draft.title: Risk and protective factors
card: Something that makes a health problem more likely to happen. Examples are smoking, social isolation and a poor diet.
Something that makes a health problem less likely, or softens its effects if it does happen. Examples are supportive friends, regular exercise and access to health care.
Factors can be personal, such as habits and beliefs, or come from a person's surroundings, such as family, school and income.
A risk factor makes a problem more likely, but it does not mean the problem will happen. A person can have several risk and protective factors at the same time.
draft.remember: Risk factors raise the chance of a health problem. Protective factors lower the chance or soften the effects.

a.q: Which of these is a protective factor for a young person's mental health?
opts: Having close friends who offer support
Spending most days alone at home
Having no one to talk to about worries
a.why: Supportive friends make poor mental health less likely and can ease its effects if it does occur. The other three make problems more likely, so they are risk factors.
a.clue: Which one lowers the chance of a problem or softens it?

b.q: Ravi, 16, lives in Bendigo. He has a family history of heart disease and eats few vegetables. He also plays football twice a week. Which statement is correct?
opts: Football protects him, but diet and family history are risks
Football and his diet both protect his heart health
His risk factors mean he will get heart disease
His protective factor removes all of his risk
b.why: Regular exercise lowers the chance of heart disease, so it is protective. A poor diet and family history raise the chance, so they are risks. Risk factors make a problem more likely but do not guarantee it, and one protective factor does not remove all risk.
b.clue: Sort each factor by whether it raises or lowers the chance, and remember neither is a guarantee.

a.best: Having close friends who offer support

b.best: Football protects him, but diet and family history are risks
